parsed.answer: This has been reported before: the Explorer "Open in Terminal" entry goes missing and reinstalling Terminal from the Store does not bring it back. This appears to be an OS-side problem with Explorer losing or not loading the shell-extension registration for packaged apps, and the tickets show no permanent fix. What the tickets suggest: (1) Restart Explorer with `taskkill /f /im explorer.exe && explorer.exe`, or reboot, because Explorer caches context menus. (2) On Windows 10, right-click directly on a folder or file rather than the empty background, because the background entry is unreliable there. The entry may still show on a folder, and Shift + right-click may also reveal it. (3) If it is still missing, add a manual registry entry under HKCR\Directory\Background\shell\terminal\command that points to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\wt.exe -d "%V\."`. (4) Submit feedback through the Feedback Hub under "Desktop Environment > Right-click context menu" and share the link in the ticket so the team can pass it to the Explorer team. Some reporters said the problem began after uninstalling PowerToys or running `winget upgrade --all`, so mention it if either applies to you.
